name: Yaman
time: Pratham prahar of ratri, just after sunset to about 9 pm
aroha: N R G M(tivra) D N Ṡ
avaroha: Ṡ N D P M(tivra) G R S
description: Yaman is one of the most fundamental ragas of Hindustani music and is often the first raga a student learns. It uses all shuddha swaras except the tivra Madhyam. Its phrases often begin with the Ni below the tonic (Ni Re Ga), and it is sung after sunset.

name: Bhairav
time: Pratham prahar of din, dawn to about 9 am
aroha: S r(komal) G M P d(komal) N Ṡ
avaroha: Ṡ N d P M G r S
description: Bhairav is a morning raga with komal Re and komal Dha. It is characterised by the slow oscillation (andolan) on the komal Dha and Re, which gives it a grave and prayerful mood.

name: Bageshri
time: Dwitiya prahar of ratri, about 9 pm to midnight
avaroha: Ṡ N(komal) D M P D M G(komal) R S
description: Bageshri is a late-night raga of longing (viraha). It uses komal Ga and komal Ni, and the Pa is used sparingly. It is popular in both khayal and light classical forms.

name: Shuddha Kalyan
aroha: S R G P D Ṡ
avaroha: Ṡ N D P M(tivra) G R S
description: A popular early night raga, Shuddha Kalyan ascends with the same five swaras as Bhupali (SRGPDS), and descends with the full seven of Yaman (SNDPMGRS), leading some to title it ‘Bhoop-Kalyan’.
